title: Find or nothing
description:
Return a pointer to a found item, or `nullptr`.

```
find("bob"): Bob, 41
find("zed"): not found
raise Bob's age through the pointer: 42
```
hints: `return &person;` inside the loop gives the address of the element itself, not a copy (lesson 1.05).
`push_back` may move every element to new memory, so old pointers to them point at freed memory.
requirements: `Person* find(std::vector<Person>& people, const std::string& name)` ignores case.
Explain in a comment why the pointer becomes dangling if `people` grows afterwards.
stretch: Return an index instead and show it survives growth.
